Subject: Inquiry: hosted API pricing for projected high throughput

Hi Ben,

We are mapping out costs for a potential shift of several inference workloads to Redwood. Rough preliminary forecast: roughly 800M to 1.2B tokens/month starting Q4, spiking to ~1.8B in some months. We're evaluating hosted API options first.

Can you send the baseline hosted API rate card and any standard volume discount schedules or committed tiers you offer? Key questions:
- Do you have a published slab/tier schedule (tokens/month -> per-token price)?
- How do you treat streaming vs non-streaming tokens for discounts?
- Are there committed usage discounts vs month-to-month flex?
- Any minimums, uplift for higher concurrency, or egress charges we should be aware of?

We want a short one-pager or spreadsheet we can show procurement. If possible, include an example math for 1B tokens/month.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Inc.

Hi Lena — thanks for the details and the projection file. This is helpful and exactly the sort of thing we use to model a recommended committed tier.

Quick answers up front:
- We have both standard published hosted API baseline rates and a separate committed-volume discount schedule.
- Streaming and non-streaming tokens are counted the same for tier thresholds; we only make small billing differences for very long-lived streaming sessions (rare).
- Committed discounts start at 3-month minimums; larger discounts require a 6–12 month commit.
- We do not charge egress on responses for our API product; there are separate fees for Dedicated/Private (networking) but not for hosted.

I'll loop in Marissa and Karthik from pricing/finance to propose a clean tiered example and a one-page proposal you can share with procurement. Expect a proper PDF + spreadsheet tomorrow.

Best,

Please see suggested approach below and add comments inline:
- Propose three committed tiers: 250M, 750M, 1.5B tokens/mo with step-down per-token prices.
- Offer a blended-monthly true-up for spike months (i.e., bill committed at discounted rate, overage billed at a modest uplift).
- Include an option for a 12-month AE (annual committed) that gives additional 10% off the committed rate.
- For streaming parity: treat all tokens equally for thresholds, but call out long-lived streaming chargebands in footnote.

Questions for finance: Is margin acceptable on 1.5B tier if we give a 20% discount off published list? Also any sensitivity on giving an introductory 90-day deeper discount?

Thanks — Ben

Subject: Redwood hosted API proposal: tiered schedule + example math (ACME-2026-06)

Hi Lena / Tom — attaching a short proposal and the editable projection spreadsheet per procurement's ask. Summary highlights below. Full attachments: Redwood_Tiered_Pricing_Proposal_v1.pdf and acme_token_projection_2026.xlsx.

Executive summary (short):
- Baseline list price for hosted generation tokens: $0.00006 per token.
- Committed tiers (monthly committed tokens, per-token committed rate):
  * Tier A: 250M -> $0.000048 (20% off list)
  * Tier B: 750M -> $0.0000425 (29.2% off list)
  * Tier C: 1.5B -> $0.000036 (40% off list)
- Overage policy: monthly usage above committed tier billed at list * 1.10 (10% uplift) to discourage unmanaged spikes; monthly true-up applied at the end of each month.
- Annual commit option: 12-month pre-commit to Tier B or C receives additional 10% off the committed per-token rate (applies to committed volumes only).
- Streaming tokens: counted equivalently for tier thresholds. We call out a footnote for sessions >30 minutes where a small operational surcharge may apply; this is uncommon and can be kept out of the commercial if desired.
- SLA/credits: standard hosted SLA is 99.9% uptime. For committed customers we can provide a custom SLA with latency SLOs and credits; I'll route to our Legal & Reliability teams on formal language if you want it in the contract.

Example math (1B tokens in a month, recommended commercial):
- Option 1 (committed Tier B at 750M):
  * Committed cost = 750,000,000 * $0.0000425 = $31,875.00
  * Overage = 250,000,000 * (list * 1.10 = $0.000066) = $16,500.00
  * Total = $48,375.00 -> effective per-token = $0.000048375
- Option 2 (commit to Tier C at 1.5B):
  * Committed cost (pro-rated for 1B use) = 1,000,000,000 * $0.000036 = $36,000.00 (if they commit to 1.5B but only consume 1B, billed on actual consumed up to committed amount)
  * Total = $36,000.00 -> effective per-token = $0.000036

Next steps:
1) If this looks directionally right, I'll prepare a formal commercial term sheet (PDF) and an editable spreadsheet with month-by-month true-up logic.
2) If Procurement wants a dedicated latency SLA and credits, I'll loop in Legal + Reliability for contract language.
3) We can provide an optional short analysis showing the delta to Private deployment per 100M tokens; note Private has infra and onboarding fees.

Requested attachments: attached. Let me know if you want a short call tomorrow to review the spreadsheet live.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
